    --bg:#111315; --panel:#181B1E; --sunk:#202428; --stage:#1A1E22; --zone:#2A271E;
    --ink:#ECEEF0; --ink2:#B7BEC5; --muted:#8B949C; --line:#2C3136;
    --accent:#D8B24C; --accent-ink:#1A1405; --accent-soft:#3A3014;
    --series:#D8B24C; --warn:#E5534B; --ok:#5BB774; color-scheme:dark;
  }
}
:root[data-theme="dark"]{
  --bg:#111315; --panel:#181B1E; --sunk:#202428; --stage:#1A1E22; --zone:#2A271E;
  --ink:#ECEEF0; --ink2:#B7BEC5; --muted:#8B949C; --line:#2C3136;
  --accent:#D8B24C; --accent-ink:#1A1405; --accent-soft:#3A3014;
  --series:#D8B24C; --warn:#E5534B; --ok:#5BB774; color-scheme:dark;
}
*{box-sizing:border-box}
body{background:var(--bg);color:var(--ink);font:15px/1.6 var(--f-body);}
.wrap{max-width:1200px;margin:0 auto;padding-left:max(16px, env(safe-area-inset-left, 0px));padding-right:max(16px, env(safe-area-inset-right, 0px));padding-block:28px 64px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:56px}
h1,h2,h3{font-family:var(--f-display);font-weight:600;letter-spacing:.01em;text-wrap:balance;margin:0;line-height:1.1}
h1{font-size:clamp(34px,5vw,52px);font-weight:700}
h2{font-size:30px}
h3{font-size:21px}
p{margin:0;max-width:68ch}
a{color:var(--accent)}
.mono{font-family:var(--f-mono)}
.eyebrow{font-family:var(--f-mono);font-size:11.5px;letter-spacing:.12em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--muted)}
.lede{color:var(--ink2);font-size:16.5px}
section{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:18px;min-width:0}
.sec-head{display:flex;align-items:baseline;gap:14px;flex-wrap:wrap;border-bottom:2px solid var(--ink);padding-bottom:8px}
.sec-head .no{font-family:var(--f-mono);font-size:13px;color:var(--accent);font-weight:500}
.tbl{overflow-x:auto;border:1px solid var(--line);background:var(--panel)}
table{border-collapse:collapse;width:100%;font-size:13.5px}
th,td{padding:8px 12px;text-align:left;vertical-align:top;border-bottom:1px solid var(--line)}
th{font-family:var(--f-mono);font-weight:500;font-size:11px;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--muted);background:var(--sunk);white-space:nowrap}
td.num,th.num{font-family:var(--f-mono);font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;white-space:nowrap}
tr:last-child td{border-bottom:0}
.hl{background:var(--accent-soft)}
th.hl{color:var(--ink)}
td .tag{font-family:var(--f-mono);font-size:11px;padding:1px 6px;border:1px solid var(--line);white-space:nowrap}
.letter{display:inline-flex;width:20px;height:20px;align-items:center;justify-content:center;border:1.5px solid var(--accent);border-radius:50%;font:600 11px var(--f-mono);color:var(--ink)}

/* grids */
.two{display:grid;grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1fr) minmax(0,1fr);gap:20px}
@media (max-width:820px){.two{grid-template-columns:1fr}}
.card{border:1px solid var(--line);background:var(--panel);padding:16px 18px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:10px;min-width:0}
ol.cycle{list-style:none;margin:0;padding:0;display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fill,minmax(230px,1fr));gap:12px;counter-reset:c}
ol.cycle li{counter-increment:c;border-top:2px solid var(--ink);padding-top:10px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:4px;font-size:14px}
ol.cycle li::before{content:"Step " counter(c);font:500 11.5px var(--f-mono);letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--accent)}
ol.cycle li b{font-family:var(--f-display);font-size:19px;font-weight:600}
.steps{list-style:none;margin:0;padding:0;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:0;border:1px solid var(--line);background:var(--panel)}
.steps>li{display:grid;grid-template-columns:64px minmax(0,1fr) auto;gap:16px;padding:16px 18px;border-bottom:1px solid var(--line);align-items:start}
.steps>li:last-child{border-bottom:0}
.steps .n{font:600 30px/1 var(--f-display);color:var(--accent)}
.steps h3{margin-bottom:4px}
.steps ul{margin:6px 0 0;padding-left:18px;font-size:14px;color:var(--ink2)}
.steps .chk{font-size:13px;margin-top:6px}
.steps .chk b{font-family:var(--f-mono);font-size:11px;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--ok)}
@media (max-width:640px){.steps>li{grid-template-columns:40px minmax(0,1fr)}.steps>li .btn{grid-column:2}}
.note{border-left:3px solid var(--warn);padding:10px 14px;background:var(--panel);font-size:14px}
.note b{color:var(--warn)}
.chartbox{position:relative;border:1px solid var(--line);background:var(--panel);padding:10px 8px 4px;overflow-x:auto}
#fchart{display:block;width:100%;min-width:560px;height:auto}
#fchart text{font-family:var(--f-mono);font-size:11px;fill:var(--muted)}
#fchart .grid{stroke:var(--line);stroke-width:1}
#fchart .axis{stroke:var(--ink2);stroke-width:1}
#fchart .line{fill:none;stroke:var(--series);stroke-width:2;stroke-linejoin:round;stroke-linecap:round}

    11

    Failure modes and Rev B fixes

    This review looked at how hand-lever badge and magnet presses fail in use, from operator guides, vendor troubleshooting pages and user reports. It then checked Rev A at the loads a person can put on the grip: 200 N for a normal push and 500 N for someone leaning on it. Each problem below has a Rev B fix in the drawings and a test that proves it.

    What goes wrong on existing presses
    • Jams from double shells or mis-loaded parts are the most common stoppage. The usual cure is a partial "kick-out" stroke on the crimp die, not force on the handle.
    • Film slips and paper shows at the edge with laser-printed photos (toner wax), heavy paper or card, or a worn crimp lead-in.
    • Cheap die sets crack or warp after a few hundred uses, and some presses arrive with the dies already out of alignment.
    • Handles that screw into soft fittings strip, and one library review reports a mechanism that sticks in the down position (both secondary reports).
    • Over-oiling soils the finished pieces. Dirt on the slide makes the table stop short of its station.
    What the Rev A stress check found
    • Handle joint: the M12 stud between bar and hub reached ≈ 465 MPa at a 200 N push and ≈ 1,160 MPa at 500 N. It would bend or snap.
    • Handle return: the two Rev A springs gave 0.8 N·m at the closed position, where the toggle needs about 4 N·m to reopen. The handle would stay down, which is the "sticks down" report above.
    • Pivot pin O (Ø12): 542 MPa at 8 kN and more than 1,000 MPa at a 16 kN overload.
    • Nothing locked the table on station. A table 2 mm off station lands the upper frame on the lower frame's edge.
    • Base (12 mm): 0.51 mm deflection at 16 kN; die walls of 1.75 mm next to counterbores in hardened steel.

    Maintenance schedule
    WhenTask
    Each shiftWipe the die table, rails and dies. Blow shell chips out of the frames. No oil on the dies.
    Weekly or 5,000 strokesCheck the thumb screws, the die lock screw and the handle-stop setting. Light oil on the rails only.

    Un-jam procedure
    1. Stop. Don't force the handle past the point where it stops.
    2. Lift the handle back to its open stop.
    3. If a shell is stuck in the upper frame, slide die B under the ram with no back plate. Make a slow partial stroke, and the plug pushes the shell out into die B.

    11

    Failure modes and Rev B fixes

    This review looked at how hand-lever badge and magnet presses fail in use, from operator guides, vendor troubleshooting pages and user reports. It then checked Rev A at the loads a person can put on the grip: 200 N for a normal push and 500 N for someone leaning on it. Each problem below has a Rev B fix in the drawings and a test that proves it.

    What goes wrong on existing presses
    • Jams from double shells or mis-loaded parts are the most common stoppage. The usual cure is a partial "kick-out" stroke on the crimp die, not force on the handle.
    • Film slips and paper shows at the edge with laser-printed photos (toner wax), heavy paper or card, or a worn crimp lead-in.
    • Cheap die sets crack or warp after a few hundred uses, and some presses arrive with the dies already out of alignment.
    • Handles that screw into soft fittings strip, and one library review reports a mechanism that sticks in the down position (both secondary reports).
    • Over-oiling soils the finished pieces. Dirt on the slide makes the table stop short of its station.
    What the Rev A stress check found
    • Handle joint: the M12 stud between bar and hub reached ≈ 465 MPa at a 200 N push and ≈ 1,160 MPa at 500 N. It would bend or snap.
    • Handle return: the two Rev A springs gave 0.8 N·m at the closed position, where the toggle needs about 4 N·m to reopen. The handle would stay down, which is the "sticks down" report above.
    • Pivot pin O (Ø12): 542 MPa at 8 kN and more than 1,000 MPa at a 16 kN overload.
    • Nothing locked the table on station. A table 2 mm off station lands the upper frame on the lower frame's edge.
    • Base (12 mm): 0.51 mm deflection at 16 kN; die walls of 1.75 mm next to counterbores in hardened steel.

    11

    Failure modes and Rev B fixes

    This review looked at how hand-lever badge and magnet presses fail in use, from operator guides, vendor troubleshooting pages and user reports. It then checked Rev A at the loads a person can put on the grip: 200 N for a normal push and 500 N for someone leaning on it. Each problem below has a Rev B fix in the drawings and a test that proves it.

    What goes wrong on existing presses
    • Jams from double shells or mis-loaded parts are the most common stoppage. The usual cure is a partial "kick-out" stroke on the crimp die, not force on the handle.
    • Film slips and paper shows at the edge with laser-printed photos (toner wax), heavy paper or card, or a worn crimp lead-in.
    • Cheap die sets crack or warp after a few hundred uses, and some presses arrive with the dies already out of alignment.
    • Handles that screw into soft fittings strip, and one library review reports a mechanism that sticks in the down position (both secondary reports).
    • Over-oiling soils the finished pieces. Dirt on the slide makes the table stop short of its station.
    What the Rev A stress check found
    • Handle joint: the M12 stud between bar and hub reached ≈ 465 MPa at a 200 N push and ≈ 1,160 MPa at 500 N. It would bend or snap.
    • Handle return: the two Rev A springs gave 0.8 N·m at the closed position, where the toggle needs about 4 N·m to reopen. The handle would stay down, which is the "sticks down" report above.
    • Pivot pin O (Ø12): 542 MPa at 8 kN and more than 1,000 MPa at a 16 kN overload.
    • Nothing locked the table on station. A table 2 mm off station lands the upper frame on the lower frame's edge.
    • Base (12 mm): 0.51 mm deflection at 16 kN; die walls of 1.75 mm next to counterbores in hardened steel.

    WhenTask

    px = im.load()
    def is_bg(c):
        return (abs(c[0]-c[1])<6 and abs(c[1]-c[2])<8 and c[0]>200)
    xs=[];ys=[]

    pad=40; x0=max(0,x0-pad); x1=min(W,x1+pad); y0=max(0,y0-pad); y1=min(H,y1+pad)
    r=111/200
    w=x1-x0; h=y1-y0

        nw=int(h*r); cx=(x0+x1)//2; x0=max(0,cx-nw//2); x1=min(W,x0+nw)
    else:
        nh=int(w/r); cy=(y0+y1)//2; y0=max(0,cy-nh//2); y1=min(H,y0+nh)

content.text:
I finished the failure review and turned it into **Rev B**, published at the same link: https://claude.ai/artifact/C4NaemzVJD5yDM3Ks2FCBi (new section 11 has the full failure-mode table). The new drawing PDF and DXF zip are attached and replace the Rev A files.

**How existing presses fail**
- **Jams from double shells** are the most common stoppage. The fix is a gentle partial stroke on the crimp die, not forcing the handle. ([ABM stuck](https://www.americanbuttonmachines.com/pages/button-maker-stuck), [ABM un-jam](https://www.americanbuttonmachines.com/blogs/american-button-machines/how-to-unjam-a-button-maker-video-tutorial))
- **Film slipping and white edges** come from laser toner, paper that is too heavy, or card. ([ABM crimping issues](https://www.americanbuttonmachines.com/blogs/american-button-machines/button-making-questions-ask-abm-common-crimping-issues-solved), [Etsy thread](https://community.etsy.com/t5/Pinback-Button-Lovers-of-Etsy/Mylar-not-crimping/td-p/35346065))
- **Cheap dies crack or warp after a few hundred uses**, and some arrive misaligned. This comes from a vendor's guide, so treat it as a viewpoint. ([MN Magnets](https://mnmagnets.com/blogs/news/fridge-magnet-machine-guide))
- **Over-oiling** soils the finished magnets. ([Nebraska maintenance guide](https://nlc.nebraska.gov/grants/innovationstudios/Documents/ButtonMaintenanceDocument.pdf))
- **Handle threads stripping and mechanisms sticking down** turned up only in search summaries. I couldn't confirm either at a primary source.

**What my stress check found wrong in Rev A**
- The M12 handle thread reached about 465 MPa at a normal 200 N push. It would have bent or snapped.
- The return springs were about 5× too weak to lift the handle from fully down, so it would have stayed down.
- The Ø12 pivot pin was overstressed if someone leans on the grip (500 N gives about 15.6 kN at the die).
- Nothing locked the table on station, so an off-station stroke would have crashed the dies.
- The die walls next to the counterbores were only 1.75 mm thick in hardened steel, and the base was thinner than it should be.

**Rev B changes (drawings, 3D model and parts lists all updated)**
1. **One-piece handle lever** (MP-113). The separate bar MP-115 is deleted. The lever is longer, so the die force rises from 5.6 to 6.2 kN at 200 N.
2. **Ø16 pivot pin** running in dry PTFE-composite bushings at all three pivots, with no grease.
3. **Return springs** of 60 N open and 225 N closed. They now lift the handle from fully down.
4. **Station pilot pin** (new part MP-120). It enters the table 6 mm before the dies meet and stops the stroke if the table is off station.
5. **Same outside size on every die set**: 126 × 100 mm for the die bodies and frames, and one shoe size. Only the plug, the pedestals and the frame openings change with magnet size. Wall thickness goes up from 1.75 mm to at least 3.25 mm.
6. **Die steel** changes from D2 to A2, which is about twice as tough. Dies get re-tempered after wire-EDM and finished with chrome. There is a PVD-coating option for high volume.
7. **Upper frame**: a lead-in edge plus four spring plungers, so the shell can't drop out while the table slides.
8. **Base and frame**: the base goes to 15 mm with rubber pads and bench-mounting holes, and the design load rises to 16 kN.
9. **Process items**: lock washers on the main nuts and screws, an adjustable handle stop, paper spec, maintenance schedule, un-jam procedure, spare-parts kit and shipping rules.

**Checks**
- All 30 sheets were rendered and checked by eye.

entries.name: TaskCreate
entries.description:
Use this tool to create a structured task list for your current coding session. This helps you track progress, organize complex tasks, and demonstrate thoroughness to the user.
It also helps the user understand the progress of the task and overall progress of their requests.

## When to Use This Tool

Use this tool proactively in these scenarios:

- Complex multi-step tasks - When a task requires 3 or more distinct steps or actions
- Non-trivial and complex tasks - Tasks that require careful planning or multiple operations
- Plan mode - When using plan mode, create a task list to track the work
- User explicitly requests todo list - When the user directly asks you to use the todo list
- User provides multiple tasks - When users provide a list of things to be done (numbered or comma-separated)
- After receiving new instructions - Immediately capture user requirements as tasks
- When you start working on a task - Mark it as in_progress BEFORE beginning work
- After completing a task - Mark it as completed and add any new follow-up tasks discovered during implementation

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Skip using this tool when:
- There is only a single, straightforward task
- The task is trivial and tracking it provides no organizational benefit
- The task can be completed in less than 3 trivial steps
- The task is purely conversational or informational

NOTE that you should not use this tool if there is only one trivial task to do. In this case you are better off just doing the task directly.

## Task Fields

- **subject**: A brief, actionable title in imperative form (e.g., "Fix authentication bug in login flow")
- **description**: What needs to be done
- **activeForm** (optional): Present continuous form shown in the spinner when the task is in_progress (e.g., "Fixing authentication bug"). If omitted, the spinner shows the subject instead.

All tasks are created with status `pending`.

## Tips

- Create tasks with clear, specific subjects that describe the outcome
- After creating tasks, use TaskUpdate to set up dependencies (blocks/blockedBy) if needed
- Check TaskList first to avoid creating duplicate tasks

subject.description: A brief title for the task

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

metadata.description: Arbitrary metadata to attach to the task

entries.name: TaskUpdate
entries.description:
Use this tool to update a task in the task list.

## When to Use This Tool

**Mark tasks as resolved:**
- When you have completed the work described in a task
- When a task is no longer needed or has been superseded
- IMPORTANT: Always mark your assigned tasks as resolved when you finish them
- After resolving, call TaskList to find your next task

- ONLY mark a task as completed when you have FULLY accomplished it
- If you encounter errors, blockers, or cannot finish, keep the task as in_progress
- When blocked, create a new task describing what needs to be resolved
- Never mark a task as completed if:
  - Tests are failing
  - Implementation is partial
  - You encountered unresolved errors
  - You couldn't find necessary files or dependencies

**Delete tasks:**
- When a task is no longer relevant or was created in error
- Setting status to `deleted` permanently removes the task

**Update task details:**
- When requirements change or become clearer
- When establishing dependencies between tasks

## Fields You Can Update

- **status**: The task status (see Status Workflow below)
- **subject**: Change the task title (imperative form, e.g., "Run tests")
- **description**: Change the task description
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")
- **owner**: Change the task owner (agent name)
- **metadata**: Merge metadata keys into the task (set a key to null to delete it)
- **addBlocks**: Mark tasks that cannot start until this one completes
- **addBlockedBy**: Mark tasks that must complete before this one can start

## Status Workflow

Status progresses: `pending` → `in_progress` → `completed`

Use `deleted` to permanently remove a task.

## Staleness

Make sure to read a task's latest state using `TaskGet` before updating it.

## Examples

Mark task as in progress when starting work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "in_progress"}
```

Mark task as completed after finishing work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "completed"}
```

Delete a task:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "deleted"}
```

Claim a task by setting owner:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "owner": "my-name"}
```

Set up task dependencies:
```json
{"taskId": "2", "addBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```

taskId.description: The ID of the task to update

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

addBlocks.description: Task IDs that this task blocks

addBlockedBy.description: Task IDs that block this task

metadata.description: Metadata keys to merge into the task. Set a key to null to delete it.

def lever_rest_height(psi=3.0, z=105.0):
    """y of the lever underside above the front column (z) at handle angle psi."""
    prof, _ = P.lever_profile()
    c, s = math.cos(math.radians(psi)), math.sin(math.radians(psi))
    best = None
    for i in range(len(prof)):
        (u0, w0), (u1, w1) = prof[i], prof[(i + 1) % len(prof)]
        for t in [k / 20.0 for k in range(21)]:
            u, w = u0 + (u1 - u0) * t, w0 + (w1 - w0) * t

def lever_rest_height(psi=3.0, z=105.0):

    prof, _ = P.lever_profile()
    c, s = math.cos(math.radians(psi)), math.sin(math.radians(psi))

"""Die-set drawings (MP-2xx), general arrangement (MP-001) and cover (MP-000).
Rev C: one universal die per press (body, carriers, station bases, springs) + a hardened size kit per magnet size."""
import math
from draft import *
import parts as P
from parts import new, SIZES, SIZE_LABEL, SHOWN, GEN, DXFS

KIT_NOTES = ['Size kit part: one per magnet size, tabulated below. Shown to scale for size 6590 (65 × 90). X = long side, along the die table.',
             'Laser-mark on a side face: drawing no., size code and U / A / B where applicable (e.g. "MP-207 6590 A").']
UNI_NOTES = ['Universal die part: one per press, the same for every magnet size. X = along the die table, +Z = front.',
             'Laser-mark the drawing number on a side face.']

# ---- Rev C universal die geometry ----
CX, CZ = 144.0, 116.0                     # carriers and upper die body, outside
RX_, RZ_ = 106.0, 81.0                    # size rings, outside (ground -0.01/-0.02)
PKX, PKZ = 106.02, 81.02                  # carrier pocket for the rings (+0.01/0)
LDX, LDZ = 96.0, 72.0                     # ledge opening under the lower rings
RET = [(sx * 62.5, sz * 49.25) for sx in (-1, 1) for sz in (-1, 1)]          # carrier shoulder screws
SPR_LOW = [(62.5, 0), (-62.5, 0), (0, 49.25), (0, -49.25)]                     # lower springs, A and B
SPR_UP = [(sx * 30, sz * 49.25) for sx in (-1, 1) for sz in (-1, 1)] + [(sx * 62.5, sz * 25) for sx in (-1, 1) for sz in (-1, 1)]
KEY = {'A': [(53.01, -20), (-53.01, 20)], 'B': [(53.01, 20), (-53.01, -20)], 'U': [(0, 40.51), (0, -40.51)]}
BASE = (150.0, 120.0)
BASE_FIX = [(sx * 35, sz * 35) for sx in (-1, 1) for sz in (-1, 1)]
BASE_DOWEL = [(45, 0), (-45, 0)]
PLUG_DOWEL = [(20, -10), (-20, -10)]
STUD = (-18, 14)
PIN_X = -11.2                              # ball-lock pin axis (along Z), 4 above the body bottom face

KIT_MAT = 'A2 / 1.2363 tool steel; 7075-T6 for the prototype kit; PM cold-work steel for high volume'
KIT_FIN = 'Harden 58–60 HRC, temper ×2; wire-EDM + 2 skim cuts, then re-temper; forming edges Ra 0.2; thin dense chrome'
CAR_MAT = '42CrMo4 (1.7225) plate, QT 28–32 HRC'
CAR_FIN = 'Black oxide; pocket walls ground or wire-EDM, Ra 0.8'


def rr_notched(w, h, r, notches, rn=2.1):
    """rounded rectangle centred at 0 with semicircular notches (rn) cut into the edges.
    notches: list of ('R'|'L'|'T'|'B', position along the edge) in plan coordinates (u, w)."""
    hw, hh = w / 2.0, h / 2.0
    segs = []
    def edge(side, a, b, fixed):
        cuts = sorted(p for (s, p) in notches if s == side)
        pos = a
        for c in cuts:
            if side in ('R', 'L'):
                segs.append(L(fixed, pos, fixed, c - rn))
                segs.append(A(fixed, c, rn, 90, 270) if side == 'R' else A(fixed, c, rn, 270, 450))
            else:
                segs.append(L(pos, fixed, c - rn, fixed))
                segs.append(A(c, fixed, rn, 180, 360) if side == 'T' else A(c, fixed, rn, 0, 180))
            pos = c + rn
        if side in ('R', 'L'):
            segs.append(L(fixed, pos, fixed, b))
        else:
            segs.append(L(pos, fixed, b, fixed))
    edge('B', -hw + r, hw - r, -hh); segs.append(A(hw - r, -hh + r, r, 270, 360))
    edge('R', -hh + r, hh - r, hw); segs.append(A(hw - r, hh - r, r, 0, 90))
    edge('T', -hw + r, hw - r, hh); segs.append(A(-hw + r, hh - r, r, 90, 180))
    edge('L', -hh + r, hh - r, -hw); segs.append(A(-hw + r, -hh + r, r, 180, 270))
    return segs


def key_notches(which):
    """key slots of a ring (plan coordinates: u = x, w = -z)."""
    out = []
    for (x, z) in KEY[which]:
        if which == 'U':
            out.append(('T' if -z > 0 else 'B', x))
        else:
            out.append(('R' if x > 0 else 'L', -z))
    return out


# ---------------- part definitions ----------------
def body(X=None, Z=None):
    f = [feat(0, 0, 'tap', m='M10', thru=True, label='S')]
    f += [feat(x, z, 'hole', d=5, depth=6, side='bot', label='D') for (x, z) in PLUG_DOWEL]
    f.append(feat(STUD[0], STUD[1], 'hole', d=10.5, depth=8, side='bot', label='K'))
    f += [feat(x, z, 'tap', m='M5', thru=True, label='R') for (x, z) in RET]
    f += [feat(x, z, 'hole', d=10.5, depth=8, side='bot') for (x, z) in SPR_UP]
    f.append(feat(0, 20, 'hole', d=4, depth=6, side='top', label='O'))
    return rrect(0, 0, CX, CZ, 6), 10, f


def upcarrier(X=None, Z=None):
    f = [feat(0, 0, 'rr', w=PKX, h=PKZ, r=6, thru=True)]
    f += [feat(x, z, 'hole', d=6.1, thru=True, cb=(10.5, 10), cbside='bot') for (x, z) in RET]
    f += [feat(x, z, 'hole', d=10.5, depth=12, side='top') for (x, z) in SPR_UP]
    f += [feat(x, z, 'hole', d=4, thru=True) for (x, z) in KEY['U']]
    return rrect(0, 0, CX, CZ, 3), 14, f


def lowcarrier(which):
    f = [feat(0, 0, 'rr', w=PKX, h=PKZ, r=6, depth=15, side='top'), feat(0, 0, 'rr', w=LDX, h=LDZ, r=6, thru=True)]
    f += [feat(x, z, 'hole', d=6.1, thru=True, cb=(10.5, 14), cbside='top') for (x, z) in RET]
    f += [feat(x, z, 'hole', d=10.5, depth=15, side='bot') for (x, z) in SPR_LOW]
    f += [feat(x, z, 'hole', d=4, depth=15, side='top') for (x, z) in KEY[which]]
    return rrect(0, 0, CX, CZ, 3), 18, f


def stbase():
    f = [feat(0, 0, 'hole', d=12, depth=8, side='top', label='C'), feat(0, 20, 'hole', d=4, depth=6, side='top', label='Q')]
    f += [feat(x, z, 'hole', d=10.5, depth=7, side='top') for (x, z) in SPR_LOW]
    f += [feat(x, z, 'tap', m='M5', thru=True) for (x, z) in RET]
    f += [feat(x, z, 'tap', m='M5', depth=8, side='bot') for (x, z) in BASE_FIX]
    f += [feat(x, z, 'hole', d=6, depth=6, side='bot') for (x, z) in BASE_DOWEL]
    return rrect(0, 0, BASE[0], BASE[1], 3), 10, f


def plug(X, Z):
    f = [feat(STUD[0], STUD[1], 'tap', m='M6', depth=10, side='top')]
    f += [feat(x, z, 'hole', d=5, depth=8, side='top') for (x, z) in PLUG_DOWEL]
    return rrect(0, 0, X + 0.3, Z + 0.3, 4.15), 14.5, f


def ring(X, Z, which):
    """size rings: U (upper, 14 high), A (pickup, 15), B (crimp guide, 15)."""
    if which == 'U':
        f = [feat(0, 0, 'rr', w=X + 0.35, h=Z + 0.35, r=4.2, thru=True)]
        T = 14
    elif which == 'A':
        f = [feat(0, 0, 'rr', w=X + 0.6, h=Z + 0.6, r=4.3, thru=True), feat(0, 0, 'rr', w=X + 12.5, h=Z + 12.5, r=6.25, depth=0.6, side='top')]
        T = 15
    else:
        f = [feat(0, 0, 'rr', w=X + 0.45, h=Z + 0.45, r=4.2, thru=True)]
        T = 15
    return rr_notched(RX_, RZ_, 6, key_notches(which)), T, f


def pick_ped(X, Z):
    f = [feat(0, 0, 'tap', m='M5', depth=6, side='top'), feat(0, 0, 'hole', d=12, depth=8.5, side='bot'), feat(0, 20, 'hole', d=4, depth=6, side='bot')]
    return rrect(0, 0, X - 0.5, Z - 0.5, 3.75), 21.8, f


def anvil(X, Z):
    f = [feat(0, 0, 'tap', m='M5', depth=6, side='top'), feat(0, 0, 'hole', d=12, depth=8.5, side='bot'), feat(0, 20, 'hole', d=4, depth=6, side='bot')]
    return rrect(0, 0, X + 0.3, Z + 0.3, 4.15), 17, f


# ---------------- common plan + sections ----------------
def plan_and_sections(sh, outline, T, fs, callouts, sec_b=None, oy=82, sec_oy=(175, 209), extent=None):
    v = View(sh, 100, oy, 1.0)
    v.segs(outline)
    draw_plan_features(v, fs)
    xs = [p for g in outline if g[0] == 'L' for p in (g[1], g[3])]
    ys = [p for g in outline if g[0] == 'L' for p in (g[2], g[4])]
    hx = extent or max(xs)
    hz = max(ys)
    v.cl_h(-hx - 5, hx + 5, 0); v.cl_v(hz + 5, -hz - 5, 0)
    sh.text(15, 18, 'PLAN (TOP) — front at bottom', 3.2, weight='bold')
    for c in callouts:
        kind = c[0]
        if kind == 'h':
            _, u1, u2, w, wd, t = c; v.hdim(u1, w, u2, w, wd, text=t)
        elif kind == 'v':
            _, w1, w2, u, ud, t = c; v.vdim(w1, u, w2, u, ud, text=t)
        elif kind == 'l':
            _, u, w, dx_, dy_, t, r = c; v.leader(u, w, dx_, dy_, t, on_circle_r=r)
    v.section_mark(-hx - 7, 0, hx + 7, 0, 'A', flip=True)
    vs = View(sh, 100, sec_oy[0], 1.0)
    draw_section(vs, solid_minus_thru((-hx, hx), fs, 0), T, fs, 0, y0=0)
    vs.vdim(0, hx, T, hx, hx + 9, text=fmt(T))
    vs.text(0, 0, 'SECTION A–A', 3.2, dy=8.5, weight='bold')
    vb = None
    if sec_b is not None:
        zc, label = sec_b
        v.section_mark(-hx - 7, -zc, hx + 7, -zc, 'B', flip=False)
        vb = View(sh, 100, sec_oy[1], 1.0)
        draw_section(vb, solid_minus_thru((-hx, hx), fs, zc), T, fs, zc, y0=0)
        vb.text(0, 0, 'SECTION B–B (' + label + ')', 3.2, dy=8.5, weight='bold')
    return v, vs, vb


def outer_dims(w, h, off=9, voff=16, top=True):
    return [('h', -w / 2, w / 2, h / 2 if top else -h / 2, (h / 2 + off) if top else -(h / 2 + off), fmt(w)),
            ('v', h / 2, -h / 2, w / 2, w / 2 + voff, fmt(h))]


def feature_table(sh, x, y, rows, title='FEATURES (positions from the part centre, +Z = front)'):
    sh.text(x, y - 2, title, 3.0, weight='bold')
    cols = [('KEY', 12, 'middle'), ('POSITIONS (X, Z)', 56, 'start'), ('FEATURE', 120, 'start')]
    return sh.table(x, y, cols, rows, size=2.5, rh=4.6)


def size_table(sh, x, y, letters):
    cw = 17.0
    cols = [('SIZE', 24, 'middle'), ('X', 13, 'end'), ('Z', 13, 'end')] + [(l[0], cw, 'end') for l in letters]
    rows = [[cd, fmt(X), fmt(Z)] + [fmt(l[2](X, Z)) for l in letters] for (cd, X, Z) in SIZES]
    sh.text(x, y - 2, 'DIMENSION TABLE (mm)', 3.0, weight='bold')
    yend = sh.table(x, y, cols, rows, size=2.7, rh=5.2, bold_first_col=True)
    yy = yend + 5
    sh.text(x, yy, 'Size code = magnet face: 5050 = 50 × 50, 6363 = 63.5 × 63.5, 5380 = 53 × 80, 6590 = 65 × 90.', 2.4)
    yy += 4.5
    for l in letters:
        sh.text(x, yy, '%s = %s' % (l[0], l[1]), 2.6)
        yy += 4.0
    return yy


def uni_sheet(no, title, outline, T, fs, callouts, rows, notes, qty, material=CAR_MAT, finish=CAR_FIN, sec_b=None, dxfname=None,
              extra=None, scale='1:1'):
    sh = new(no, title, scale=scale, qty=qty, material=material, finish=finish, notes=UNI_NOTES + notes + GEN)
    v, vs, vb = plan_and_sections(sh, outline, T, fs, callouts, sec_b, oy=84, sec_oy=(184, 214))
    if extra:
        extra(sh, v, vs, vb)
    feature_table(sh, 212, 26, rows)
    if dxfname:
        dx = DXF(); dx.segs(outline); feats_dxf(dx, fs); DXFS['%s_%s.dxf' % (no, dxfname)] = dx
    return sh


def kit_sheet(no, title, fn, letters, notes, callouts, feat_rows, extra=None, sec_b=None, dxfname=None, qty='1 per size kit (4)',
              material=KIT_MAT, finish=KIT_FIN):
    sh = new(no, title, scale='1:1 (size 6590)', qty=qty, material=material, finish=finish, notes=KIT_NOTES + notes + GEN)
    code, X, Z = SHOWN
    outline, T, fs = fn(X, Z)
    v, vs, vb = plan_and_sections(sh, outline, T, fs, callouts, sec_b)
    if extra:
        extra(sh, v, vs, vb)
    yy = size_table(sh, 212, 24, letters)
    if feat_rows:
        feature_table(sh, 212, yy + 6, feat_rows)
    if dxfname:
        for (cd, x, z) in SIZES:
            o, T_, f_ = fn(x, z)
            dx = DXF(); dx.segs(o); feats_dxf(dx, f_)
            DXFS['%s_%s_%s.dxf' % (no, dxfname, cd)] = dx
    return sh


RET_T = '(±62.5, ±49.25)'
SPL_T = '(±62.5, 0), (0, ±49.25)'
SPU_T = '(±30, ±49.25), (±62.5, ±25)'


# ---------------- universal die ----------------
def mp201():
    outline, T, fs = body()
    def extra(sh, v, vs, vb):
        for dx_ in (-3, 3):
            v.line(PIN_X + dx_, -CZ / 2, PIN_X + dx_, -6, 'hid')
        v.cl_v(-CZ / 2 - 3, -4, PIN_X)
        v.leader(PIN_X, -40, -46, 30, 'L: Ø6 H8 from the FRONT face to Z = +6,\n4 above the bottom face (ball-lock pin)')
    uni_sheet('MP-201', 'UPPER DIE BODY (UNIVERSAL)', outline, T, fs,

                                    ('l', 0, 0, 92, 10, 'S: M10 THRU (shank)', 4.25)],
              [['S', 'centre', 'M10 THRU (shank MP-202, Loctite 243)'],
               ['D', '(±20, −10)', 'Ø5 H7 × 6 from the BOTTOM (plug dowels)'],
               ['K', '(−18, +14)', 'Ø10.5 × 8 from the BOTTOM (plug stud MP-212)'],
               ['L', 'X −11.2, Z +58 → +6', 'Ø6 H8 along Z, 4 above the bottom face (ball-lock pin Ø6, grip ≥ 55)'],
               ['R', RET_T, 'M5 THRU (carrier shoulder screws ISO 7379 Ø6 × 10)'],
               ['P', SPU_T, 'Ø10.5 × 8 from the BOTTOM (8 upper springs)'],
               ['O', '(0, +20)', 'Ø4 H7 × 6 from the TOP (orientation pin Ø4 m6 × 10)']],
              ['Rev C: one body per press (144 × 116). The plug now hangs on dowels D and the stud K, held by a Ø6 ball-lock pin in hole L: no screws to change a size.',
               'Top face (seat against the holder through the shim pack) and bottom face parallel 0.01, flat 0.01. The shim pack sets the crimp depth once for all kits.',
               'Upper springs: 8 × ISO 10243 Ø10 × 32 blue in 26 mm cavities: 6 mm preload (≈ 0.68 kN total), ≈ 1.3 kN at full retraction (36%). Replace every 250,000 strokes.'],
              '1 per press', material='1.2312 (P20+S) prehardened 28–32 HRC', finish='Black oxide', sec_b=(49.25, 'Z = ±49.25'),

def mp202():
    sh = new('MP-202', 'UPPER DIE SHANK', scale='4:1', qty='1 per press',
             material='42CrMo4 Ø20 bar, QT 28–32 HRC', finish='Black oxide',
             notes=['Screw into the die body MP-201 (M10 THRU) with Loctite 243 until the Ø16 face seats; face square to axis 0.01.',

def mp205():

    uni_sheet('MP-210', 'UPPER CARRIER (UNIVERSAL)', outline, T, fs,

                                    ('v', PKZ / 2, -PKZ / 2, -PKX / 2 + 15, -CX / 2 - 12, fmt(PKZ) + ' +0.01/0')],
              [['W', 'centre', 'Pocket 106.02 × 81.02 (+0.01/0), R6, THRU: holds the upper ring MP-204'],
               ['R', RET_T, 'Ø6.1 THRU, CBORE Ø10.5 × 10 from the BOTTOM'],
               ['P', SPU_T, 'Ø10.5 × 12 from the TOP (8 upper springs)'],
               ['K', '(0, ±40.51)', 'Ø4 H7 THRU on the pocket wall; press in Ø4 m6 × 14 flush (key pins, upper ring only)'],

"""Die-set drawings (MP-2xx), general arrangement (MP-001) and cover (MP-000).
Rev C: one universal die per press (body, carriers, station bases, springs) + a hardened size kit per magnet size."""
import math
from draft import *
import parts as P
from parts import new, SIZES, SIZE_LABEL, SHOWN, GEN, DXFS

KIT_NOTES = ['Size kit part: one per magnet size, tabulated below. Shown to scale for size 6590 (65 × 90). X = long side, along the die table.',
             'Laser-mark on a side face: drawing no., size code and U / A / B where applicable (e.g. "MP-207 6590 A").']
UNI_NOTES = ['Universal die part: one per press, the same for every magnet size. X = along the die table, +Z = front.',
             'Laser-mark the drawing number on a side face.']

# ---- Rev C universal die geometry ----
CX, CZ = 144.0, 116.0                     # carriers and upper die body, outside
RX_, RZ_ = 106.0, 81.0                    # size rings, outside (ground -0.01/-0.02)
PKX, PKZ = 106.02, 81.02                  # carrier pocket for the rings (+0.01/0)
LDX, LDZ = 96.0, 72.0                     # ledge opening under the lower rings
RET = [(sx * 62.5, sz * 49.25) for sx in (-1, 1) for sz in (-1, 1)]          # carrier shoulder screws
SPR_LOW = [(62.5, 0), (-62.5, 0), (0, 49.25), (0, -49.25)]                     # lower springs, A and B
SPR_UP = [(sx * 30, sz * 49.25) for sx in (-1, 1) for sz in (-1, 1)] + [(sx * 62.5, sz * 25) for sx in (-1, 1) for sz in (-1, 1)]
KEY = {'A': [(53.01, -20), (-53.01, 20)], 'B': [(53.01, 20), (-53.01, -20)], 'U': [(0, 40.51), (0, -40.51)]}
BASE = (150.0, 120.0)
BASE_FIX = [(sx * 35, sz * 35) for sx in (-1, 1) for sz in (-1, 1)]
BASE_DOWEL = [(45, 0), (-45, 0)]
PLUG_DOWEL = [(20, -10), (-20, -10)]
STUD = (-18, 14)
PIN_X = -11.2                              # ball-lock pin axis (along Z), 4 above the body bottom face

KIT_MAT = 'A2 / 1.2363 tool steel; 7075-T6 for the prototype kit; PM cold-work steel for high volume'
KIT_FIN = 'Harden 58–60 HRC, temper ×2; wire-EDM + 2 skim cuts, then re-temper; forming edges Ra 0.2; thin dense chrome'
CAR_MAT = '42CrMo4 (1.7225) plate, QT 28–32 HRC'
CAR_FIN = 'Black oxide; pocket walls ground or wire-EDM, Ra 0.8'


def rr_notched(w, h, r, notches, rn=2.1):
    """rounded rectangle centred at 0 with semicircular notches (rn) cut into the edges.
    notches: list of ('R'|'L'|'T'|'B', position along the edge) in plan coordinates (u, w)."""
    hw, hh = w / 2.0, h / 2.0
    segs = []
    def edge(side, a, b, fixed):
        cuts = sorted(p for (s, p) in notches if s == side)
        pos = a
        for c in cuts:
            if side in ('R', 'L'):
                segs.append(L(fixed, pos, fixed, c - rn))
                segs.append(A(fixed, c, rn, 90, 270) if side == 'R' else A(fixed, c, rn, 270, 450))
            else:
                segs.append(L(pos, fixed, c - rn, fixed))
                segs.append(A(c, fixed, rn, 180, 360) if side == 'T' else A(c, fixed, rn, 0, 180))
            pos = c + rn
        if side in ('R', 'L'):
            segs.append(L(fixed, pos, fixed, b))
        else:
            segs.append(L(pos, fixed, b, fixed))
    edge('B', -hw + r, hw - r, -hh); segs.append(A(hw - r, -hh + r, r, 270, 360))
    edge('R', -hh + r, hh - r, hw); segs.append(A(hw - r, hh - r, r, 0, 90))
    edge('T', -hw + r, hw - r, hh); segs.append(A(-hw + r, hh - r, r, 90, 180))
    edge('L', -hh + r, hh - r, -hw); segs.append(A(-hw + r, -hh + r, r, 180, 270))
    return segs


def key_notches(which):
    """key slots of a ring (plan coordinates: u = x, w = -z)."""
    out = []
    for (x, z) in KEY[which]:
        if which == 'U':
            out.append(('T' if -z > 0 else 'B', x))
        else:
            out.append(('R' if x > 0 else 'L', -z))
    return out


# ---------------- part definitions ----------------
def body(X=None, Z=None):
    f = [feat(0, 0, 'tap', m='M10', thru=True, label='S')]
    f += [feat(x, z, 'hole', d=5, depth=6, side='bot', label='D') for (x, z) in PLUG_DOWEL]
    f.append(feat(STUD[0], STUD[1], 'hole', d=10.5, depth=8, side='bot', label='K'))
    f += [feat(x, z, 'tap', m='M5', thru=True, label='R') for (x, z) in RET]
    f += [feat(x, z, 'hole', d=10.5, depth=8, side='bot') for (x, z) in SPR_UP]
    f.append(feat(0, 20, 'hole', d=4, depth=6, side='top', label='O'))
    return rrect(0, 0, CX, CZ, 6), 10, f


def upcarrier(X=None, Z=None):
    f = [feat(0, 0, 'rr', w=PKX, h=PKZ, r=6, thru=True)]
    f += [feat(x, z, 'hole', d=6.1, thru=True, cb=(10.5, 10), cbside='bot') for (x, z) in RET]
    f += [feat(x, z, 'hole', d=10.5, depth=12, side='top') for (x, z) in SPR_UP]
    f += [feat(x, z, 'hole', d=4, thru=True) for (x, z) in KEY['U']]
    return rrect(0, 0, CX, CZ, 3), 14, f


def lowcarrier(which):
    f = [feat(0, 0, 'rr', w=PKX, h=PKZ, r=6, depth=15, side='top'), feat(0, 0, 'rr', w=LDX, h=LDZ, r=6, thru=True)]
    f += [feat(x, z, 'hole', d=6.1, thru=True, cb=(10.5, 14), cbside='top') for (x, z) in RET]
    f += [feat(x, z, 'hole', d=10.5, depth=15, side='bot') for (x, z) in SPR_LOW]
    f += [feat(x, z, 'hole', d=4, depth=15, side='top') for (x, z) in KEY[which]]
    return rrect(0, 0, CX, CZ, 3), 18, f


def stbase():
    f = [feat(0, 0, 'hole', d=12, depth=8, side='top', label='C'), feat(0, 20, 'hole', d=4, depth=6, side='top', label='Q')]
    f += [feat(x, z, 'hole', d=10.5, depth=7, side='top') for (x, z) in SPR_LOW]
    f += [feat(x, z, 'tap', m='M5', thru=True) for (x, z) in RET]
    f += [feat(x, z, 'tap', m='M5', depth=8, side='bot') for (x, z) in BASE_FIX]
    f += [feat(x, z, 'hole', d=6, depth=6, side='bot') for (x, z) in BASE_DOWEL]
    return rrect(0, 0, BASE[0], BASE[1], 3), 10, f

    return rrect(0, 0, X + 0.3, Z + 0.3, 4.15), 14.5, f


def ring(X, Z, which):
    """size rings: U (upper, 14 high), A (pickup, 15), B (crimp guide, 15)."""
    if which == 'U':
        f = [feat(0, 0, 'rr', w=X + 0.35, h=Z + 0.35, r=4.2, thru=True)]
        T = 14
    elif which == 'A':
        f = [feat(0, 0, 'rr', w=X + 0.6, h=Z + 0.6, r=4.3, thru=True), feat(0, 0, 'rr', w=X + 12.5, h=Z + 12.5, r=6.25, depth=0.6, side='top')]
        T = 15
    else:
        f = [feat(0, 0, 'rr', w=X + 0.45, h=Z + 0.45, r=4.2, thru=True)]
        T = 15
    return rr_notched(RX_, RZ_, 6, key_notches(which)), T, f

# ---------------- common plan + sections ----------------
def plan_and_sections(sh, outline, T, fs, callouts, sec_b=None, oy=82, sec_oy=(175, 209), extent=None):
    v = View(sh, 100, oy, 1.0)
    v.segs(outline)
    draw_plan_features(v, fs)
    xs = [p for g in outline if g[0] == 'L' for p in (g[1], g[3])]
    ys = [p for g in outline if g[0] == 'L' for p in (g[2], g[4])]
    hx = extent or max(xs)
    hz = max(ys)
    v.cl_h(-hx - 5, hx + 5, 0); v.cl_v(hz + 5, -hz - 5, 0)
    sh.text(15, 18, 'PLAN (TOP) — front at bottom', 3.2, weight='bold')
    for c in callouts:
        kind = c[0]
        if kind == 'h':
            _, u1, u2, w, wd, t = c; v.hdim(u1, w, u2, w, wd, text=t)
        elif kind == 'v':
            _, w1, w2, u, ud, t = c; v.vdim(w1, u, w2, u, ud, text=t)
        elif kind == 'l':
            _, u, w, dx_, dy_, t, r = c; v.leader(u, w, dx_, dy_, t, on_circle_r=r)
    v.section_mark(-hx - 7, 0, hx + 7, 0, 'A', flip=True)
    vs = View(sh, 100, sec_oy[0], 1.0)
    draw_section(vs, solid_minus_thru((-hx, hx), fs, 0), T, fs, 0, y0=0)
    vs.vdim(0, hx, T, hx, hx + 9, text=fmt(T))
    vs.text(0, 0, 'SECTION A–A', 3.2, dy=8.5, weight='bold')
    vb = None
    if sec_b is not None:
        zc, label = sec_b
        v.section_mark(-hx - 7, -zc, hx + 7, -zc, 'B', flip=False)
        vb = View(sh, 100, sec_oy[1], 1.0)
        draw_section(vb, solid_minus_thru((-hx, hx), fs, zc), T, fs, zc, y0=0)
        vb.text(0, 0, 'SECTION B–B (' + label + ')', 3.2, dy=8.5, weight='bold')
    return v, vs, vb


def outer_dims(w, h, off=9, voff=16, top=True):
    return [('h', -w / 2, w / 2, h / 2 if top else -h / 2, (h / 2 + off) if top else -(h / 2 + off), fmt(w)),
            ('v', h / 2, -h / 2, w / 2, w / 2 + voff, fmt(h))]


def feature_table(sh, x, y, rows, title='FEATURES (positions from the part centre, +Z = front)'):
    sh.text(x, y - 2, title, 3.0, weight='bold')
    cols = [('KEY', 12, 'middle'), ('POSITIONS (X, Z)', 56, 'start'), ('FEATURE', 120, 'start')]
    return sh.table(x, y, cols, rows, size=2.5, rh=4.6)


def size_table(sh, x, y, letters):
    cw = 17.0
    cols = [('SIZE', 24, 'middle'), ('X', 13, 'end'), ('Z', 13, 'end')] + [(l[0], cw, 'end') for l in letters]
    rows = [[cd, fmt(X), fmt(Z)] + [fmt(l[2](X, Z)) for l in letters] for (cd, X, Z) in SIZES]
    sh.text(x, y - 2, 'DIMENSION TABLE (mm)', 3.0, weight='bold')
    yend = sh.table(x, y, cols, rows, size=2.7, rh=5.2, bold_first_col=True)
    yy = yend + 5
    sh.text(x, yy, 'Size code = magnet face: 5050 = 50 × 50, 6363 = 63.5 × 63.5, 5380 = 53 × 80, 6590 = 65 × 90.', 2.4)
    yy += 4.5
    for l in letters:
        sh.text(x, yy, '%s = %s' % (l[0], l[1]), 2.6)
        yy += 4.0
    return yy


def uni_sheet(no, title, outline, T, fs, callouts, rows, notes, qty, material=CAR_MAT, finish=CAR_FIN, sec_b=None, dxfname=None,
              extra=None, scale='1:1'):
    sh = new(no, title, scale=scale, qty=qty, material=material, finish=finish, notes=UNI_NOTES + notes + GEN)
    v, vs, vb = plan_and_sections(sh, outline, T, fs, callouts, sec_b, oy=84, sec_oy=(184, 214))
    if extra:
        extra(sh, v, vs, vb)
    feature_table(sh, 212, 26, rows)
    if dxfname:
        dx = DXF(); dx.segs(outline); feats_dxf(dx, fs); DXFS['%s_%s.dxf' % (no, dxfname)] = dx
    return sh


def kit_sheet(no, title, fn, letters, notes, callouts, feat_rows, extra=None, sec_b=None, dxfname=None, qty='1 per size kit (4)',
              material=KIT_MAT, finish=KIT_FIN):
    sh = new(no, title, scale='1:1 (size 6590)', qty=qty, material=material, finish=finish, notes=KIT_NOTES + notes + GEN)
    code, X, Z = SHOWN
    outline, T, fs = fn(X, Z)
    v, vs, vb = plan_and_sections(sh, outline, T, fs, callouts, sec_b)
    if extra:
        extra(sh, v, vs, vb)
    yy = size_table(sh, 212, 24, letters)
    if feat_rows:
        feature_table(sh, 212, yy + 6, feat_rows)
    if dxfname:
        for (cd, x, z) in SIZES:
            o, T_, f_ = fn(x, z)
            dx = DXF(); dx.segs(o); feats_dxf(dx, f_)
            DXFS['%s_%s_%s.dxf' % (no, dxfname, cd)] = dx
    return sh

"""Die-set drawings (MP-2xx), general arrangement (MP-001) and cover (MP-000).
Rev C: one universal die per press (body, carriers, station bases, springs) + a hardened size kit per magnet size."""
import math
from draft import *
import parts as P
from parts import new, SIZES, SIZE_LABEL, SHOWN, GEN, DXFS

KIT_NOTES = ['Size kit part: one per magnet size, tabulated below. Shown to scale for size 6590 (65 × 90). X = long side, along the die table.',
             'Laser-mark on a side face: drawing no., size code and U / A / B where applicable (e.g. "MP-207 6590 A").']
UNI_NOTES = ['Universal die part: one per press, the same for every magnet size. X = along the die table, +Z = front.',
             'Laser-mark the drawing number on a side face.']

# ---- Rev C universal die geometry ----
CX, CZ = 144.0, 116.0                     # carriers and upper die body, outside
RX_, RZ_ = 106.0, 81.0                    # size rings, outside (ground -0.01/-0.02)
PKX, PKZ = 106.02, 81.02                  # carrier pocket for the rings (+0.01/0)
LDX, LDZ = 96.0, 72.0                     # ledge opening under the lower rings
RET = [(sx * 62.5, sz * 49.25) for sx in (-1, 1) for sz in (-1, 1)]          # carrier shoulder screws
SPR_LOW = [(62.5, 0), (-62.5, 0), (0, 49.25), (0, -49.25)]                     # lower springs, A and B
SPR_UP = [(sx * 30, sz * 49.25) for sx in (-1, 1) for sz in (-1, 1)] + [(sx * 62.5, sz * 25) for sx in (-1, 1) for sz in (-1, 1)]
KEY = {'A': [(53.01, -20), (-53.01, 20)], 'B': [(53.01, 20), (-53.01, -20)], 'U': [(0, 40.51), (0, -40.51)]}
BASE = (150.0, 120.0)
BASE_FIX = [(sx * 35, sz * 35) for sx in (-1, 1) for sz in (-1, 1)]
BASE_DOWEL = [(45, 0), (-45, 0)]
PLUG_DOWEL = [(20, -10), (-20, -10)]
STUD = (-18, 14)
PIN_X = -11.2                              # ball-lock pin axis (along Z), 4 above the body bottom face

KIT_MAT = 'A2 / 1.2363 tool steel; 7075-T6 for the prototype kit; PM cold-work steel for high volume'
KIT_FIN = 'Harden 58–60 HRC, temper ×2; wire-EDM + 2 skim cuts, then re-temper; forming edges Ra 0.2; thin dense chrome'
CAR_MAT = '42CrMo4 (1.7225) plate, QT 28–32 HRC'
CAR_FIN = 'Black oxide; pocket walls ground or wire-EDM, Ra 0.8'


def rr_notched(w, h, r, notches, rn=2.1):
    """rounded rectangle centred at 0 with semicircular notches (rn) cut into the edges.
    notches: list of ('R'|'L'|'T'|'B', position along the edge) in plan coordinates (u, w)."""
    hw, hh = w / 2.0, h / 2.0
    segs = []
    def edge(side, a, b, fixed):
        cuts = sorted(p for (s, p) in notches if s == side)
        pos = a
        for c in cuts:
            if side in ('R', 'L'):
                segs.append(L(fixed, pos, fixed, c - rn))
                segs.append(A(fixed, c, rn, 90, 270) if side == 'R' else A(fixed, c, rn, 270, 450))
            else:
                segs.append(L(pos, fixed, c - rn, fixed))
                segs.append(A(c, fixed, rn, 180, 360) if side == 'T' else A(c, fixed, rn, 0, 180))
            pos = c + rn
        if side in ('R', 'L'):
            segs.append(L(fixed, pos, fixed, b))
        else:
            segs.append(L(pos, fixed, b, fixed))
    edge('B', -hw + r, hw - r, -hh); segs.append(A(hw - r, -hh + r, r, 270, 360))
    edge('R', -hh + r, hh - r, hw); segs.append(A(hw - r, hh - r, r, 0, 90))
    edge('T', -hw + r, hw - r, hh); segs.append(A(-hw + r, hh - r, r, 90, 180))
    edge('L', -hh + r, hh - r, -hw); segs.append(A(-hw + r, -hh + r, r, 180, 270))
    return segs


def key_notches(which):
    """key slots of a ring (plan coordinates: u = x, w = -z)."""
    out = []
    for (x, z) in KEY[which]:
        if which == 'U':
            out.append(('T' if -z > 0 else 'B', x))
        else:
            out.append(('R' if x > 0 else 'L', -z))
    return out


# ---------------- part definitions ----------------
def body(X=None, Z=None):
    f = [feat(0, 0, 'tap', m='M10', thru=True, label='S')]
    f += [feat(x, z, 'hole', d=5, depth=6, side='bot', label='D') for (x, z) in PLUG_DOWEL]
    f.append(feat(STUD[0], STUD[1], 'hole', d=10.5, depth=8, side='bot', label='K'))
    f += [feat(x, z, 'tap', m='M5', thru=True, label='R') for (x, z) in RET]
    f += [feat(x, z, 'hole', d=10.5, depth=8, side='bot') for (x, z) in SPR_UP]
    f.append(feat(0, 20, 'hole', d=4, depth=6, side='top', label='O'))
    return rrect(0, 0, CX, CZ, 6), 10, f


def upcarrier(X=None, Z=None):
    f = [feat(0, 0, 'rr', w=PKX, h=PKZ, r=6, thru=True)]
    f += [feat(x, z, 'hole', d=6.1, thru=True, cb=(10.5, 10), cbside='bot') for (x, z) in RET]
    f += [feat(x, z, 'hole', d=10.5, depth=12, side='top') for (x, z) in SPR_UP]
    f += [feat(x, z, 'hole', d=4, thru=True) for (x, z) in KEY['U']]
    return rrect(0, 0, CX, CZ, 3), 14, f


def lowcarrier(which):
    f = [feat(0, 0, 'rr', w=PKX, h=PKZ, r=6, depth=15, side='top'), feat(0, 0, 'rr', w=LDX, h=LDZ, r=6, thru=True)]
    f += [feat(x, z, 'hole', d=6.1, thru=True, cb=(10.5, 14), cbside='top') for (x, z) in RET]
    f += [feat(x, z, 'hole', d=10.5, depth=15, side='bot') for (x, z) in SPR_LOW]
    f += [feat(x, z, 'hole', d=4, depth=15, side='top') for (x, z) in KEY[which]]
    return rrect(0, 0, CX, CZ, 3), 18, f


def stbase():
    f = [feat(0, 0, 'hole', d=12, depth=8, side='top', label='C'), feat(0, 20, 'hole', d=4, depth=6, side='top', label='Q')]
    f += [feat(x, z, 'hole', d=10.5, depth=7, side='top') for (x, z) in SPR_LOW]
    f += [feat(x, z, 'tap', m='M5', thru=True) for (x, z) in RET]
    f += [feat(x, z, 'tap', m='M5', depth=8, side='bot') for (x, z) in BASE_FIX]
    f += [feat(x, z, 'hole', d=6, depth=6, side='bot') for (x, z) in BASE_DOWEL]
    return rrect(0, 0, BASE[0], BASE[1], 3), 10, f


def plug(X, Z):
    f = [feat(STUD[0], STUD[1], 'tap', m='M6', depth=10, side='top')]
    f += [feat(x, z, 'hole', d=5, depth=8, side='top') for (x, z) in PLUG_DOWEL]
    return rrect(0, 0, X + 0.3, Z + 0.3, 4.15), 14.5, f


def ring(X, Z, which):
    """size rings: U (upper, 14 high), A (pickup, 15), B (crimp guide, 15)."""
    if which == 'U':
        f = [feat(0, 0, 'rr', w=X + 0.35, h=Z + 0.35, r=4.2, thru=True)]
        T = 14
    elif which == 'A':
        f = [feat(0, 0, 'rr', w=X + 0.6, h=Z + 0.6, r=4.3, thru=True), feat(0, 0, 'rr', w=X + 12.5, h=Z + 12.5, r=6.25, depth=0.6, side='top')]
        T = 15
    else:
        f = [feat(0, 0, 'rr', w=X + 0.45, h=Z + 0.45, r=4.2, thru=True)]
        T = 15
    return rr_notched(RX_, RZ_, 6, key_notches(which)), T, f


def pick_ped(X, Z):
    f = [feat(0, 0, 'tap', m='M5', depth=6, side='top'), feat(0, 0, 'hole', d=12, depth=8.5, side='bot'), feat(0, 20, 'hole', d=4, depth=6, side='bot')]
    return rrect(0, 0, X - 0.5, Z - 0.5, 3.75), 21.8, f


def anvil(X, Z):
    f = [feat(0, 0, 'tap', m='M5', depth=6, side='top'), feat(0, 0, 'hole', d=12, depth=8.5, side='bot'), feat(0, 20, 'hole', d=4, depth=6, side='bot')]
    return rrect(0, 0, X + 0.3, Z + 0.3, 4.15), 17, f


# ---------------- common plan + sections ----------------
def plan_and_sections(sh, outline, T, fs, callouts, sec_b=None, oy=82, sec_oy=(175, 209), extent=None):
    v = View(sh, 100, oy, 1.0)
    v.segs(outline)
    draw_plan_features(v, fs)
    xs = [p for g in outline if g[0] == 'L' for p in (g[1], g[3])]
    ys = [p for g in outline if g[0] == 'L' for p in (g[2], g[4])]
    hx = extent or max(xs)
    hz = max(ys)
    v.cl_h(-hx - 5, hx + 5, 0); v.cl_v(hz + 5, -hz - 5, 0)
    sh.text(15, 18, 'PLAN (TOP) — front at bottom', 3.2, weight='bold')
    for c in callouts:
        kind = c[0]
        if kind == 'h':
            _, u1, u2, w, wd, t = c; v.hdim(u1, w, u2, w, wd, text=t)
        elif kind == 'v':
            _, w1, w2, u, ud, t = c; v.vdim(w1, u, w2, u, ud, text=t)
        elif kind == 'l':
            _, u, w, dx_, dy_, t, r = c; v.leader(u, w, dx_, dy_, t, on_circle_r=r)
    v.section_mark(-hx - 7, 0, hx + 7, 0, 'A', flip=True)
    vs = View(sh, 100, sec_oy[0], 1.0)
    draw_section(vs, solid_minus_thru((-hx, hx), fs, 0), T, fs, 0, y0=0)
    vs.vdim(0, hx, T, hx, hx + 9, text=fmt(T))
    vs.text(0, 0, 'SECTION A–A', 3.2, dy=8.5, weight='bold')
    vb = None
    if sec_b is not None:
        zc, label = sec_b
        v.section_mark(-hx - 7, -zc, hx + 7, -zc, 'B', flip=False)
        vb = View(sh, 100, sec_oy[1], 1.0)
        draw_section(vb, solid_minus_thru((-hx, hx), fs, zc), T, fs, zc, y0=0)
        vb.text(0, 0, 'SECTION B–B (' + label + ')', 3.2, dy=8.5, weight='bold')
    return v, vs, vb


def outer_dims(w, h, off=9, voff=16, top=True):
    return [('h', -w / 2, w / 2, h / 2 if top else -h / 2, (h / 2 + off) if top else -(h / 2 + off), fmt(w)),
            ('v', h / 2, -h / 2, w / 2, w / 2 + voff, fmt(h))]


def feature_table(sh, x, y, rows, title='FEATURES (positions from the part centre, +Z = front)'):
    sh.text(x, y - 2, title, 3.0, weight='bold')
    cols = [('KEY', 12, 'middle'), ('POSITIONS (X, Z)', 56, 'start'), ('FEATURE', 120, 'start')]
    return sh.table(x, y, cols, rows, size=2.5, rh=4.6)


def size_table(sh, x, y, letters):
    cw = 17.0
    cols = [('SIZE', 24, 'middle'), ('X', 13, 'end'), ('Z', 13, 'end')] + [(l[0], cw, 'end') for l in letters]
    rows = [[cd, fmt(X), fmt(Z)] + [fmt(l[2](X, Z)) for l in letters] for (cd, X, Z) in SIZES]
    sh.text(x, y - 2, 'DIMENSION TABLE (mm)', 3.0, weight='bold')
    yend = sh.table(x, y, cols, rows, size=2.7, rh=5.2, bold_first_col=True)
    yy = yend + 5
    sh.text(x, yy, 'Size code = magnet face: 5050 = 50 × 50, 6363 = 63.5 × 63.5, 5380 = 53 × 80, 6590 = 65 × 90.', 2.4)
    yy += 4.5
    for l in letters:
        sh.text(x, yy, '%s = %s' % (l[0], l[1]), 2.6)
        yy += 4.0
    return yy


def uni_sheet(no, title, outline, T, fs, callouts, rows, notes, qty, material=CAR_MAT, finish=CAR_FIN, sec_b=None, dxfname=None,
              extra=None, scale='1:1'):
    sh = new(no, title, scale=scale, qty=qty, material=material, finish=finish, notes=UNI_NOTES + notes + GEN)
    v, vs, vb = plan_and_sections(sh, outline, T, fs, callouts, sec_b, oy=84, sec_oy=(184, 214))
    if extra:
        extra(sh, v, vs, vb)
    feature_table(sh, 212, 26, rows)
    if dxfname:
        dx = DXF(); dx.segs(outline); feats_dxf(dx, fs); DXFS['%s_%s.dxf' % (no, dxfname)] = dx
    return sh


def kit_sheet(no, title, fn, letters, notes, callouts, feat_rows, extra=None, sec_b=None, dxfname=None, qty='1 per size kit (4)',
              material=KIT_MAT, finish=KIT_FIN):
    sh = new(no, title, scale='1:1 (size 6590)', qty=qty, material=material, finish=finish, notes=KIT_NOTES + notes + GEN)
    code, X, Z = SHOWN
    outline, T, fs = fn(X, Z)
    v, vs, vb = plan_and_sections(sh, outline, T, fs, callouts, sec_b)
    if extra:
        extra(sh, v, vs, vb)
    yy = size_table(sh, 212, 24, letters)
    if feat_rows:
        feature_table(sh, 212, yy + 6, feat_rows)
    if dxfname:

	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

## Lovable
Lovable is an AI-powered full-stack app builder. The AI agent edits TypeScript + Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui code in a cloud sandbox with a live preview.

New projects use Lovable's backend default stack. There is no tech stack selector in `create_project`; include framework or rendering preferences in the initial message.

What Lovable can build:
- Landing pages, dashboards, SaaS apps, internal tools, marketplaces, and more
- Full-stack apps with authentication (Supabase Auth), databases (PostgreSQL), file storage, and edge functions
- Apps with payments (Stripe), email (Resend), AI features, and 20+ integrations
- See https://docs.lovable.dev/integrations/introduction for the full integration catalog

How to interact:
- Use create_project with initial_message and workspace_id. If multiple workspaces are possible, create_project returns available_workspaces; choose one or ask the user, then call create_project again with workspace_id. After create_project returns projectId, call render_project_widget with that projectId to show build progress.
- Send natural-language messages via send_message — describe what you want built or changed
- send_message and create_project initial messages send work from the MCP client's AI agent to Lovable's AI agent on the user's behalf and consume the user's workspace credits.
- The agent reads your project's code, makes edits, and rebuilds the preview automatically
- Attach images (designs, screenshots, wireframes) via file uploads to guide visual implementation
- Use plan_mode=true on send_message to discuss approach before the agent writes code
- Iterate: review changes with get_diff, then send follow-up messages to refine
- A result with status 'awaiting_input' and an awaiting_input object means the agent paused on a tool approval. Show the human awaiting_input.tool_id and awaiting_input.params when present, ask for their decision, then call respond_to_approval with that awaiting_input's event_id and the user message_id the pause was reported on (from send_message, create_project, or the get_message you polled; not the assistant message id). Do not answer a pause with send_message; that rejects the pending tool. If awaiting_input.requires_secure_form is true, do not ask for the decision or any value: give the user awaiting_input.editor_url, tell them to answer there, and never ask for or accept a credential in this conversation.

Each project has two URLs:
- editor_url: The Lovable editor where users visually edit their project
- preview_url: Live preview of the app, rebuilt after each agent response. Share this with users.

Knowledge & skills: Use set_project_knowledge / set_workspace_knowledge for persistent instructions. Use workspace skill tools to create, update, and delete reusable agent skills; skill management requires workspace admin/owner access.

Connectors & integrations: Use list_connectors to see which integrations (Stripe, Supabase, Shopify, Slack, etc.) are available in a workspace. Use add_connector to connect external services (Linear, Notion, custom MCP servers) so the agent can call them during chat. See https://docs.lovable.dev/integrations/introduction for the full list.

Code inspection: After sending a message, use get_diff with the message_id to see what the agent changed.
- list_files / read_file: Browse the project file tree at any commit (use latest_commit_sha from get_project)
- list_edits: Browse the project's edit history

Cloud database: Each project can have a PostgreSQL database (powered by Supabase). Use get_database_status to check, enable_database to provision, then query_database to run SQL.

Analytics: Published projects have visitor analytics.
- get_project_analytics: Historical metrics (visitors, pageviews, bounce rate, session duration) with breakdowns by page, source, device, and country.
- get_project_analytics_trend: Real-time visitor count and 5-minute interval data for the last 30 minutes.

Note: Workspaces do not have a dedicated URL. There is no link to a specific workspace.

Public API: For programmatic access outside of MCP (listing, publ… [truncated]

## Vercel
Vercel MCP provides over 200 tools. Capabilities:
Deployments: builds, status/logs/files, aliases, promotions, rollbacks, rolling releases and sharing/access.
Insights: runtime errors/logs, Web Analytics, observability metrics, usage/billing and agent run traces.
Configuration: projects, accounts/teams/access groups, environment variables, domains/pricing/registration, DNS/TLS, routes/redirects, microfrontends, feature flags, Blob stores and Global Config (Edge Config).
Platform: cache artifacts/invalidation, Marketplace integrations, Connect, firewall/protection, KMS, Vercel CI/checks, Sandbox sessions/commands/files/snapshots, drains, webhook inspection and account events.
Collaboration: Toolbar comments, Claude imports when enabled and documentation search.

Use tool input schemas. Reuse known team/project IDs and connection scope; never guess. Discover only missing scope; ask if the target remains ambiguous.

For failed deployments, inspect state and build logs. For production errors, start with get_runtime_errors, then get_runtime_logs.

Use supported project/deployment/environment/time filters. Follow pagination for complete results; report partial data. Inspect every result. Distinguish observed failures from suspected causes.

Verify changes before reporting completion. Check uncertain writes before retrying. For requires_user_action, return the dashboard URL and leave the action pending.

For access/not-found errors, verify scope and follow reported login/SSO steps.

If MCP fails or lacks an operation, use CLI fallbacks in results, tool descriptions or _meta["vercel.com/cli"]. Follow their mappings and preserve known scope; CLI credentials and defaults are separate.

Never request or print credentials, secrets or private keys. Never decrypt environment values unless requested.

    • 304
  • Marking: shoe A has a green band and is laser-marked "A · PICKUP". Shoe B has a red band and "B · CRIMP". Each part carries its drawing number and size code, for example MP-207 6590 A. The long side of every rectangular die runs along the table.

  • Standard (Rev B): A2 / 1.2363, vacuum hardened to 58–60 HRC. Wire-EDM the profiles with two skim cuts, then re-temper to remove the brittle recast layer. Polish the forming edges to Ra 0.2 µm and finish with thin dense chrome. Rev A's D2 wears better but is about half as tough, and on these dies the corners crack long before they wear out.
    • 311
  • High volume: a powder-metallurgy cold-work steel tempered high (above 500 °C), then PVD TiCN or TiAlN. The coating stops tin picking up on the frames. PVD runs at about 450 °C, so it needs a steel that is tempered above that.
    • 312
  • Prototype: 7075-T6 aluminium, CNC machined and hard anodised. This is the cheapest way to prove the fits. Expect faster wear on the forming edges.
    • 313
  • Shoes: 6061-T6 or C45. Springs: ISO 10243 Ø10: L25 blue on the upper frame, L32 green for A, L32 red for B. They work between 12.5% and 37.5% of free length; replace them every 250,000 strokes.

Fits are starting values. Upper frame opening = shell + 0.35 mm, so it grips the wrapped shell by friction. Plug = shell + 0.30 mm, sliding in the frame. Crimp frame opening = shell + 0.45 mm. Lap the upper frame opening on the first prototype until a wrapped shell lifts out of die A reliably and pushes out cleanly over die B. 05

Swappable die sets

Common interface, same on all four sets
  • Upper die: Ø16 g6 shank with a V-groove, fitted into the Ø16 H7 die holder and locked by one M5 cone-point screw. A Ø4 pin in the die top fixes the rotation, which matters for rectangles. A shim pack on each upper die sets its depth once, so swapping needs no adjustment.
  • Lower dies: each sits on a 150 × 120 × 10 shoe with two Ø8 dowels and two M5 thumb screws (head Ø12 at most). Shoe A's dowels are 80 mm apart at the back; shoe B's are 60 mm apart at the front.
  • Same outside on every size (Rev B): the upper die body, upper frame and both lower frames are 126 × 100 for all four sizes, with the same screw, spring and dowel patterns. Only the plug, the pedestals and the frame openings change with size. One CNC program covers them all, spares fit every set, and every set gets the same spring cavities.
  • Marking: shoe A has a green band and is laser-marked "A · PICKUP". Shoe B has a red band and "B · CRIMP". Each part carries its drawing number and size code, for example MP-207 6590 A. The long side of every rectangular die runs along the table.
Materials
  • Standard (Rev B): A2 / 1.2363, vacuum hardened to 58–60 HRC. Wire-EDM the profiles with two skim cuts, then re-temper to remove the brittle recast layer. Polish the forming edges to Ra 0.2 µm and finish with thin dense chrome. Rev A's D2 wears better but is about half as tough, and on these dies the corners crack long before they wear out.
  • High volume: a powder-metallurgy cold-work steel tempered high (above 500 °C), then PVD TiCN or TiAlN. The coating stops tin picking up on the frames. PVD runs at about 450 °C, so it needs a steel that is tempered above that.
  • Prototype: 7075-T6 aluminium, CNC machined and hard anodised. This is the cheapest way to prove the fits. Expect faster wear on the forming edges.
  • Shoes: 6061-T6 or C45. Springs: ISO 10243 Ø10: L25 blue on the upper frame, L32 green for A, L32 red for B. They work between 12.5% and 37.5% of free length; replace them every 250,000 strokes.

Fits are starting values. Upper frame opening = shell + 0.35 mm, so it grips the wrapped shell by friction. Plug = shell + 0.30 mm, sliding in the frame. Crimp frame opening = shell + 0.45 mm. Lap the upper frame opening on the first prototype until a wrapped shell lifts out of die A reliably and pushes out cleanly over die B. Rev B adds a 0.6 × 20° lead-in on the upper frame's bottom edge and four nylon-tip spring plungers that keep the wrapped shell from dropping out while the table slides.

Consumables per die set

The search didn't return the ISO 10243 standard itself. The results are manufacturer catalogue listings, and they consistently use the same deflection tiers for heavy-load red die springs.

- **Berger Tools (R-series, heavy load):** Each listing gives three working levels: 20% of free length for long spring life, 25% for medium spring life, and 30% as the maximum operating deflection. For example, the R20-305 is rated at 61 mm for long life and 91.5 mm at maximum, on a 305 mm free length. (Recommended Working Deflection Long Spring Life 20%; Maximum Operating Deflection 30%)
- **Essentra Components:** Its listings give an "optimum operating deflection" and a "maximum operating deflection" rather than percentages. For the 127 mm free-length spring, the optimum is 25.4 mm (20%) and the maximum operating deflection is 38.1 mm (30%). (Optimum Operating Deflection 25.4 mm, Overall Length 127.0 mm; Maximum Operating Deflection 38.1 mm) The 89 mm spring follows the same pattern. One Essentra listing, for a 25 mm free-length spring, gives an optimum of 22.3 mm, which doesn't fit the 20% pattern, so it may be a data error.

So the commonly published guidance for heavy-load red die springs is about 20% of free length for long life, about 25% for medium life, and a 30% maximum. Verify this against the ISO 10243 text or the manufacturer's datasheet before designing to it.

content.content:
A hand-lever toggle press with a sliding two-station die table. It makes square and rectangular photo fridge magnets in two strokes, and its four die sets swap without tools. This page has the 3D model, the force analysis, die and frame dimensions, a parts list, the manufacturing route, assembly steps, test plan and a failure review (section 11) that drove the Rev B changes.

The required force for each die set is an estimate: about 7 N per mm of magnet edge for the crimp spring preload, scaled from the round-badge spring figures in US 4,696,086, then × 2.2 for the final crimp. Measure it on the prototype with a load cell (section 10). Stroke 1 needs much less force and stops at about 35.5 mm, when the plug meets the shell.

Machine-shop drawings: Rev B drawing set MP-000 to MP-209 (30 A3 sheets, PDF) with DXF profiles for cutting and wire-EDM. MP-115 is deleted and MP-120 is new. Where this page and the drawings differ, the drawings govern.

Dies, productionSaw A2 (1.2363) → CNC rough with 0.3 mm left → vacuum harden, gas quench, temper twice → 58–60 HRC → wire EDM the profiles: main cut + 2 skim cuts → re-temper 25 °C below the last temper → surface grind → polish forming edges and lead-ins → thin dense chrome 3–5 µm. High volume: PM steel tempered high, then PVD TiCN / TiAlNProfile ±0.01; no recast layer on forming edges (etch check); plug-to-frame sliding fit 0.02–0.03 per side; forming edges Ra 0.2 Depth (per die set)Fit the shims so the crimp finishes with the handle about 5–10° above horizontal. Record the shim value on the upper die.Full crimp with a firm push; no hard knock at the bottom

This review looked at how hand-lever badge and magnet presses fail in use, from operator guides, vendor troubleshooting pages and user reports. It then checked Rev A at the loads a person can put on the grip: 200 N for a normal push and 500 N for someone leaning on it. Each problem below has a Rev B fix in the drawings and a test that proves it.

8Die springs break or sagWorked past 40% of free length; cavities differed by sizeFrames stop returning; pickup or crimp failsMMISO 10243 Ø10 springs at ≤ 37.5%; same cavities on every set; replace at 250,000Stroke counter; free-length check
  • A2 vs D2 (Sakysteel) and MW Alloys: toughness against wear resistance.

    • Kit parts: A2 / 1.2363 at 58–60 HRC. Wire-EDM with two skim cuts, then re-temper to remove the brittle recast layer. Polish the forming edges to Ra 0.2 and finish with thin dense chrome. For high volume, use PM steel tempered above 500 °C with PVD TiCN or TiAlN. For the prototype kit, use 7075-T6.
    • Universal die: carriers in 42CrMo4 QT, body in 1.2312, bases in C45, all black oxide. The ring pockets are made to +0.01/0 and the rings to −0.01/−0.02.

    Fits are starting values. Upper ring opening = shell + 0.35 mm, so it grips the wrapped shell by friction; the plug = shell + 0.30 mm and slides in it. The crimp ring opening = shell + 0.45 mm. Lap the upper ring on the first prototype kit until a wrapped shell lifts out of station A reliably and pushes out cleanly at station B. The upper ring has a 0.6 × 20° lead-in and four nylon-tip spring plungers that stop the wrapped shell dropping out while the table slides.

    Why not one stepped die for every size?

    What a stepped die would need, and why Rev C does it differently
    • The sizes don't stack. A step can only sit inside a bigger step. The 63.5 square is 10.5 mm taller than 53 × 80, and 53 × 80 is 16.5 mm longer than the square, so those two can't both be steps of one die.
    • Walls too thin. Even where sizes do stack (50 × 50 inside 53 × 80), the wall between two forming edges would be 1.3–1.5 mm of hardened steel. That is the corner-cracking failure from section 11.
    • Steps get in the way. The edge of a big shell has to roll under its back plate, and a smaller step's ledge sits right where that edge has to go. In the plug, the joint between steps would print a line across the big magnet's photo.
    • What Rev C keeps from the idea: one die does the work for every size, and a universal ledge in each carrier supports every ring from below. Only the thin forming "steps" (the kit rings, pedestals and plug) change, each with its own exact 0.35–0.45 mm fit.

    05

    One die, four size kits

    Rev C splits the die into two groups. The universal die is made once and stays on the press: the upper die body, the spring-loaded upper carrier, two lower carriers, two station bases and all the springs. A size kit holds only the six hardened parts that touch the shell: the plug, the upper ring, the pickup ring and pedestal, and the crimp ring and anvil. Every kit ring has the same 106 × 81 outside, so one carrier pocket takes every size, and only the openings change.

    How a size change works (about a minute, no tools)
    • Upper: loosen two thumb screws and the upper ring drops out from below. Pull the ball-lock pin and the plug comes off its two dowels. The new plug only fits one way.
    • Lower: screw the T-handle puller into the pedestal or anvil and lift it out. Then lift the ring out by its opening. Drop in the new ring, then the new pedestal or anvil on its spigot.
    • Keys: pins in each carrier match slots in its rings. A pickup ring won't seat in the crimp carrier, and a lower ring won't fit the upper carrier.
    • Depth: every kit part is made to the same heights, so the shim pack set once on the press suits every size.
    Materials and springs
    • Kit parts: A2 / 1.2363 at 58–60 HRC. Wire-EDM with two skim cuts, then re-temper to remove the brittle recast layer. Polish the forming edges to Ra 0.2 and finish with thin dense chrome. For high volume, use PM steel tempered above 500 °C with PVD TiCN or TiAlN. For the prototype kit, use 7075-T6.
    • Universal die: carriers in 42CrMo4 QT, body in 1.2312, bases in C45, all black oxide. The ring pockets are made to +0.01/0 and the rings to −0.01/−0.02.
    • Springs (Rev C, same for every size): upper, 8 × ISO 10243 Ø10 × 32 blue, about 0.68 kN preload rising to 1.3 kN. Lower, 4 × Ø10 × 32 green per carrier, 75 N rising to 0.38 kN at the stop. Every spring stays within its colour's life limit; replace them every 250,000 strokes.

    Fits are starting values. Upper ring opening = shell + 0.35 mm, so it grips the wrapped shell by friction; the plug = shell + 0.30 mm and slides in it. The crimp ring opening = shell + 0.45 mm. Lap the upper ring on the first prototype kit until a wrapped shell lifts out of station A reliably and pushes out cleanly at station B. The upper ring has a 0.6 × 20° lead-in and four nylon-tip spring plungers that stop the wrapped shell dropping out while the table slides.

    Why not one stepped die for every size?

    What a stepped die would need, and why Rev C does it differently
    • The sizes don't stack. A step can only sit inside a bigger step. The 63.5 square is 10.5 mm taller than 53 × 80, and 53 × 80 is 16.5 mm longer than the square, so those two can't both be steps of one die.
    • Walls too thin. Even where sizes do stack (50 × 50 inside 53 × 80), the wall between two forming edges would be 1.3–1.5 mm of hardened steel. That is the corner-cracking failure from section 11.
    • Steps get in the way. The edge of a big shell has to roll under its back plate, and a smaller step's ledge sits right where that edge has to go. In the plug, the joint between steps would print a line across the big magnet's photo.
    • What Rev C keeps from the idea: one die does the work for every size, and a universal ledge in each carrier supports every ring from below. Only the thin forming "steps" (the kit rings, pedestals and plug) change, each with its own exact 0.35–0.45 mm fit.

Every kit ring has the same 106 × 81 outside, so one carrier pocket takes every size, and only the openings change.

    How a size change works (about a minute, no tools)
    • Upper: loosen two thumb screws and the upper ring drops out from below. Pull the ball-lock pin and the plug comes off its two dowels. The new plug only fits one way.
    • Lower: screw the T-handle puller into the pedestal or anvil and lift it out. Then lift the ring out by its opening. Drop in the new ring, then the new pedestal or anvil on its spigot.
    • Keys: pins in each carrier match slots in its rings. A pickup ring won't seat in the crimp carrier, and a lower ring won't fit the upper carrier.
    • Depth: every kit part is made to the same heights, so the shim pack set once on the press suits every size.

content.text:
Rev C is done and is the final product design. The build pack is updated at the same link, https://claude.ai/artifact/C4NaemzVJD5yDM3Ks2FCBi, and the drawing set (33 A3 sheets plus 38 DXF profiles) is attached; it replaces the Rev B files.

**Your stepped-die idea:** I worked it through and didn't use it as a single stepped die, because it can't work for these four sizes:
- **The sizes don't stack.** The 63.5 square is 10.5 mm taller than 53 × 80, and 53 × 80 is 16.5 mm longer than the square, so they can't both be steps of one die. The page has a to-scale drawing showing the overlap.
- **The walls would crack.** Even where sizes do stack, the wall between two steps would be only 1.3–1.5 mm of hardened steel.
- **The steps get in the way.** A smaller step's ledge sits exactly where a bigger shell's edge must roll under its back plate, and the joint between steps would print a line across the bigger magnet's photo.

**What I built instead keeps the goal: one die for every size.**
- **Universal die:** made once and stays on the press — the die body, the spring-loaded carriers, the bases and all the springs. Each carrier has a ledge that supports every size from below, which covers your "support for larger sizes" point.
- **Size kit:** only six small hardened parts change per size: the plug, upper ring, pickup ring and pedestal, crimp ring and anvil. Every ring has the same 106 × 81 outside.
- **Size change:** about a minute, with no tools beyond a T-handle puller that comes with each kit. The upper ring comes off with 2 thumb screws, the plug with 1 push-button pin, and the lower parts lift out. Key pins stop a ring going into the wrong station.
- **New sizes:** any shape up to 90 × 65 is just a new kit. Each kit is also much cheaper than a full Rev B die set.

**Two mistakes in my Rev B, now fixed:**
- **Crimp springs over their limit.** I had specified red springs compressed to 37.5% of their length, but heavy-duty springs are only rated to about 30% ([Berger](https://www.berger-tools.co.uk/Die_Springs/R_-_Red_Die_Spring_Iso10243_-_Heavy_Load/PartPage/R20-305/)). Rev C uses one set of green and blue springs for every size, all within their life limits. Rates come from [Lesjöfors](https://shop.lesjofors.com/at/en-US/all-products/compression-springs/1-10032-5093/) and the [Accu chart](https://accu-components.com/us/p/496-die-spring-color-charts).
- **No crimp.** The flat crimp pedestal had nothing to turn the shell edge under the back plate, so magnets would have come apart. The new crimp anvil has a small curved channel that rolls the edge under.

**Checks:**
- All the new die sheets were rendered and checked.
- The page loads with no errors, the 3D press cycle runs with the new die, and it fits a phone screen.

**Before production:**
- Build a 7075 aluminium prototype kit first. The roll-channel shape and the spring forces are starting values to tune there before cutting tool steel.
- Have a mechanical engineer check my calculations.
